pages.title: 2.1 Basic Neuromechanics & Energy Systems
pages.readingHtml:
Neuromechanical Foundations

Human movement requires the coordinated interaction of the nervous system and the musculoskeletal system. Skeletal muscles act as active motors pulling on bony levers across joint axes.

Bioenergetic Systems

Muscular contraction is powered by ATP hydrolysis via three interconnected energy systems:

  • ATP-PCr: Immediate high-power substrate for short-duration maximal efforts (< 10 seconds).
  • Glycolytic: Anaerobic degradation of glucose producing rapid ATP and lactate (10–120 seconds).
  • Oxidative / Aerobic: Mitochondrial respiration utilizing carbohydrates and fats for prolonged, sustained work.
